title: VACUUM FULL not detecting free pages correctly
description: The compact_and_truncate() method in src/pager/pagefile.rs is checking page.page_type() == PageType::Free to identify free pages (line 1227), but pages freed by regular vacuum may not have their type updated to Free. They're tracked in the freelist but still have their original page type. This causes VACUUM FULL to not find any free pages to compact, resulting in zero pages moved and zero bytes reclaimed. Solution: Check if page is in the freelist instead of checking page type, or ensure regular vacuum updates page types to Free.
close_reason: Fixed VACUUM FULL free page detection to use freelist as source of truth. The original code read pages from disk and checked page_type() == PageType::Free, but the freelist is the authoritative source for which pages are available. Added FreeList::snapshot_free_pages() to get all free pages from the in-memory freelist. Updated compact_and_truncate() to use snapshot_free_pages() instead of disk reads. This is more efficient and handles cases where pages are in the freelist but disk state may be inconsistent.

title: Fix nondeterministic transaction ordering in WAL recovery

title: Optimize BTree split operations for better concurrent write throughput
description:
## Problem

The OLTP stress test (test_oltp_workload) shows that under extreme concurrent write load (8 threads × 200 ops × 30% writes = 480 expected), the system achieves only ~14% of expected throughput (67 writes in 300s).

## Root Cause

The BTree implementation uses optimistic concurrency control with per-leaf latching (insert_internal), which works well. However, split operations (split_and_propagate, insert_into_parent) are NOT latched, causing:

1. Validation failures during concurrent splits
2. Retries in insert_internal when path changes
3. Severe throughput degradation under high contention

## Current Behavior

- insert_internal: Uses optimistic traversal + leaf latch (good)
- split_and_propagate: No latching (causes conflicts)
- insert_into_parent: No latching (causes conflicts)

When multiple threads trigger splits on the same path, they interfere with each other, causing validation failures and retries.

## Proposed Solution

Add latching to split operations:

1. Acquire latches on parent nodes during split propagation
2. Use latch coupling when inserting into parent
3. Maintain optimistic reads for non-modifying operations

This would allow concurrent splits on different paths while preventing conflicts on the same path.

## Impact

- Current: ~14% throughput under extreme load (acceptable for correctness)
- Expected after fix: 50-80% throughput under extreme load
- Real-world impact: Most workloads don't have 8 threads hammering the same small key space

## References

- tests/end_to_end_stress_tests.rs::test_oltp_workload
- src/table/btree/paged.rs::split_and_propagate
- src/table/btree/paged.rs::insert_into_parent
- docs/BTREE_CONCURRENCY_ISSUES.md
- docs/BTREE_LATCH_COUPLING_SAFE_IMPLEMENTATION.md

3. Store tombstones with (series_key, timestamp, value_key) tuples
4. Update scan_series() to filter out tombstoned points
5. Periodically clean up tombstones during compaction/maintenance

This will ensure that failed transactions don't leave phantom data points in time series that could corrupt analytics and queries.

Alternatively, consider implementing a versioned time series structure that supports logical deletion of points.

title: Implement true streaming with ValueRef for BTree (Priority 3)
description:
Implement true streaming with ValueRef for BTree to avoid loading large values into memory.

Current State: PagedBTree uses default streaming implementations that load full values. get_stream() calls get() which loads full value then wraps in SliceValueStream. put_stream() buffers entire stream into Vec before storing.

Problem: For large values this defeats streaming purpose causing excessive memory consumption, allocation pressure, limited concurrency, and poor performance.

Required Changes: 1) Modify VersionChain to store ValueRef instead of Vec, 2) Implement true get_stream() using OverflowChainStream, 3) Implement true put_stream() with direct overflow allocation, 4) Update BTree node serialization, 5) Update vacuum to free overflow pages.

Impact: Significant architectural change affecting core MVCC system, BTree serialization, LSM tree, and pager integration.

Implementation Plan: See docs/BTREE_VALUEREF_STREAMING_PLAN.md for detailed analysis and phased approach.

Priority: Priority 4 Backlog - Performance optimization deferred until after v1 due to high risk and wide impact.

Related: Closed nanokv-hc5 as duplicate. Infrastructure exists: OverflowChainStream, ValueRef type. See VALUEREF_STREAMING_ARCHITECTURE.md
